title: [Enhancement] Improving Warp Movement Mechanics for Greater Precision
summary: **Improving Warp Movement Mechanics for Greater Precision** I read about the optimization that allows ships to exit warp travel precisely at the edge of a gravity well or warp inhibitor field. By looking back at the ship's entry point into the prohibited area and retroactively calculating its sublight movement, the next game update can land the ship right at the boundary—combining warp travel up to that exact limit with a small amount of sublight movement beyond it. Could this same logic be applied to let ships drop out of warp at any exact target location? In the current implementation, the game drops ships out of warp well before their destination because a single game update might otherwise overshoot the target. However, using the logic above, the system could detect that an update would push the ship past its destination at warp speed, step back in time to the exact point the ship crossed the target location, drop it out of warp right there, and transition smoothly to sublight. Instead of dropping out 7,500 units early, ships could drop out 200 units early. **The Problem with Waypoint Travel** This precision is especially valuable for waypoint travel, which is currently sluggish for groups of ships. Fleets drop out of warp far from their waypoint, crawl the remaining distance at sublight, and then spin their warp engines back up. That interim sublight phase wastes a tremendous amount of time. Consider launching fighters from a carrier and queueing a waypoint attack-move command to flank the enemy fleet: 1. The fighters enter warp and reach the flank quickly (within seconds). 2. Because of the early drop-out, they spend another 15 frustrating seconds crawling at sublight to reach the exact waypoint coordinate before executing the linked attack-move command. 3.
